policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'such fornication as is not even among the Gentiles' with no verb of naming; the added ὀνομάζεται would require 'is not even named among the Gentiles', which the ASV does not have.

ἀρθῇ and the compounded ἐξαρθῇ both yield ASV 'might be taken away from among you'; the English does not distinguish the simplex from the compound. The two notes are alternative_rendering and bear on punctuation of the clauses, not on the reading.
ποιήσας and πράξας are synonymous aorist participles, both rendered 'he that had done this deed'; ASV wording cannot separate them and no note is mapped to this unit.

ASV has plain 'being absent in body but present in spirit'; the ὡς it does render ('as though I were present') belongs to the later ὡς παρών. A ὡς on ἀπών would give 'as absent in body', which the ASV does not show.
ASV reads 'in the name of our Lord Jesus' with no 'Christ'; the added Χριστοῦ would appear as 'our Lord Jesus Christ'.
ASV reads 'with the power of our Lord Jesus' with no 'Christ'; the added Χριστοῦ would appear as 'our Lord Jesus Christ'.
ASV text reads 'in the day of the Lord Jesus', rendering the added Ἰησοῦ, and the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities omit Jesus' shows the ASV knowingly printed the longer reading.
ASV reads 'For our passover also hath been sacrificed, even Christ' with nothing answering to ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν; that addition would require an explicit 'for us'.

ASV begins the verse 'not at all meaning with the fornicators' with no coordinating 'and'; the ASV renders καί here elsewhere in the chapter even sentence-initially (v.2 'And ye are puffed up'), so its absence answers to the shorter οὐ. The mapped note is alternative_rendering ('not altogether') and concerns οὐ πάντως in English, not the reading.
ASV reads 'with the covetous and extortioners', rendering καί; the variant ἢ would give 'or extortioners', which the ASV does not have.
ὠφείλετε and ὀφείλετε differ only in augment (imperfect vs present); ASV 'for then must ye needs go out of the world' is tenseless in this idiom and marks neither, and no note is mapped to the unit.

ASV reads 'For what have I to do with judging them that are without?' with nothing answering to the added καί; the longer reading would show as 'also' in the ASV, which renders καί consistently in this chapter.
ASV reads 'But them that are without God judgeth' — a present; the accented future κρινεῖ would give 'will judge'.
ASV reads the bare imperative 'Put away the wicked man from among yourselves'; the variant Καὶ ἐξαρεῖτε is a future indicative with a conjunction and would give 'And ye shall put away'.
